recent.text: I think there is a pathway to moving Yoshida if the Red Sox eat a chunk of the money. Paying $10 million or so for one year of an elite contact hitter isn't crazy, even if he can't his lefties or play the field There is no pathway to moving Story. I can't imagine there is a team
recent.author: Daniel Fox

recent.text: If MLB institutes a salary floor, Yoshida and Story would be ideal candidates for teams looking to add salary given their expiring contracts. That might be the only scenario where the Red Sox can move them
recent.author: Daniel Fox

recent.text: The point Lou made after this clip was the most important one: “What happened to blaming the players for not executing?” This has been the problem all season. Everything’s always Breslows fault or Tracy’s fault, but sometimes, the players just aren’t good enough It’s on Duran
recent.author: Daniel Fox

recent.text: Initially both Taylor Smith and Mike Groopman were listed as Red Sox people being interviewed for the opening. Smith was hired by Breslow in October of 2024. He was the Director of Predictive Modeling with the Rays. Now an Assistant GM. Key analytical voice in the front office.
recent.author: Tyler Milliken
recent.quoted_text: Boston assistant general manager Taylor Smith remains a top candidate to take over as head of baseball operations for the A’s, sources tell ESPN. Cardinals assistant GM Rob Cerfolio, another finalist, is expected to remain with St. Louis.

recent.text: The idea that the Red Sox should extend Rutschman just because they traded a bunch of prospects for him is inaccurate. The more accurate statement is that the Red Sox shouldn't let someone they felt that convicted about walk out of the door after a year and two months
recent.author: Daniel Fox

recent.text: Obviously it's not Whitlock's fault the Red Sox couldn't diagnose a broken leg, but it's just more evidence that it would foolish to move him back to the starting rotation. Keeping him healthy is more important than squeezing another 75 innings out of him
